decisions.reason: As a core extension of the firm's secure second-channel communication offering, management is likely to interpret any weaker visibility as integration into broader solutions rather than a reason to withdraw it.

Mobile digital signing remains close to the firm's announced direction toward app-based interactions and online contract signing, so prior investment and public strategic fit still favor continuation.
This end-to-end security architecture is highly central to the firm's technical core and likely embodies substantial sunk R&D, which strongly supports ongoing commitment.

Although more specialized and therefore more exposed to pruning, it still fits the secure messaging trajectory and management can plausibly attribute limited visibility to packaging or adoption timing rather than failure.
The hardware token is the least aligned with the firm's broader software-led ecosystem direction, so after several years management is more likely to let it go despite earlier investment.

The compliance suite leverages the firm's security and regulatory strengths, and in a growing market management would typically continue backing such a strategically adjacent offering rather than exit quickly.
